note: Static candidates from /vuln-scan. Confidence is scanner self-reported (Step 3b per-finding rescoring skipped at this scale); /triage performs the rigorous N-vote verification.

findings.title: Customer chat hard-limit counter is read-modify-write, not atomic — concurrent turns bypass the cap
findings.description: enforceCustomerLimit reads counter.current_count, computes nextCount = current+1, then writes via plain UPDATE on (user_id,tenant_id) with no CAS and no DB-atomic increment. Hard-tier decision is made against the stale read. K concurrent requests all read N, all pass the cap check, all proceed to paid AI calls.
findings.exploit_scenario: Authenticated customer at count=hard_cap-1 fires K parallel chat requests; each passes the gate and calls the paid model, exceeding the per-period hard ceiling and inflating tenant AI cost.
findings.recommendation: Replace read-modify-write with an atomic increment RPC (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET current_count = current_count + 1 RETURNING current_count) and decide the cap against the returned value (consume-then-check). Mirror increment_tenant_ai_cost.

findings.title: Public chat rate limit is per-instance in-memory, not shared/Redis
findings.description: Only abuse control on the unauthenticated public chat endpoint is checkRateLimit() backed by a module-level Map (30 msgs/token/hour). No middleware, no Redis limiter. On Vercel each instance has its own map; limit scales with instance count and resets on cold start. Each allowed request triggers a paid Anthropic completion + supervisor pass.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker with one valid quote/itinerary token spreads requests across the autoscaled fleet, bypassing 30/hr and driving unbounded paid LLM spend (cost-DoS).
findings.recommendation: Move public-chat rate limiting to the shared Redis limiter, keyed by token AND source IP, before the LLM call.

findings.title: Anonymous chat limit: check and increment are separate non-atomic steps
findings.description: Anon path calls checkAnonLimit (read) then incrementAnonCounters (read-then-write per identifier; code comment calls it 'atomically(ish)'). No CAS / DB-side increment, so concurrent requests collide on both the check→increment gap and the increment's own read→write gap.
findings.exploit_scenario: Unauthenticated client fires N parallel requests on a fresh session/IP/fingerprint; all pass, all call the model, counters converge below N — the free-tier signup wall is bypassed for many paid turns.
findings.recommendation: Atomic ON CONFLICT increment RPC returning post-increment value; reject when it exceeds the cap (consume-then-check). Back anon limits with Redis.

findings.title: AI-cost hard-state gate reads a 30s-cached snapshot and transitions to 'hard' fire-and-forget
findings.description: Hard-state refusal reads ai_cost_state from a 30s in-process Map cache; the transition to 'hard' is dispatched fire-and-forget (void) AFTER the call completes. State flip lags every call, stays stale up to 30s, and is per-instance. The cost increment itself is atomic but enforcement lags.
findings.exploit_scenario: Tenant at the hard threshold bursts turns; the async flip + ≤30s stale per-instance cache let dozens-hundreds of paid calls execute past the hard ceiling before any instance sees 'hard'.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the hard cap against fresh ledger state at call time (uncached read, or have increment_tenant_ai_cost return cumulative cents and reject on crossing) and await the hard-boundary transition. Soft tiers may stay cached.

findings.title: transitionCommissionState validates against a stale read and writes without a status CAS guard
findings.description: Reads current status, asserts valid transition, then UPDATEs with .eq('id',commissionId) only — no .eq('status',from) and no row-count assert. Two concurrent transitions both read 'received', both validate, both write (last-writer-wins). Underlying enabler of F-pay-01.
findings.exploit_scenario: Two operations on the same commission interleave (concurrent cancel, or cancel racing an Inngest path); an invalid-from-current-state transition is silently applied and clawback side effects proceed.
findings.recommendation: Make the write a CAS: chain .eq('status',from).select('id') and assert one row via safeAwaitRowCount; throw a typed conflict on zero rows.

findings.title: SSRF via admin-stored RSS feed URL fetched server-side with no scheme/IP allowlist or redirect guard
findings.description: fetchFeedItems(url) calls fetch() on a URL read from news_feeds.url, stored by POST /api/admin/travel-news/feeds whose only validation is new URL(body.url) — accepts file:, http://169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, *.internal, any port. No scheme allowlist, no link-local/metadata/RFC1918 block, follows redirects by default. Parsed item text/links are persisted and surfaced in UI (semi-blind SSRF).
findings.exploit_scenario: A platform admin (or anyone who can write a news_feeds row) stores url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role>; next 6-hour cron fetches it from inside the deployment network and persists fragments into travel-news items.
findings.recommendation: Enforce https-only scheme allowlist; resolve host and reject loopback/link-local/RFC1918/.internal (re-validate post-DNS for rebinding); redirect:'manual' with per-hop re-validation; consider an operator host allowlist. Centralize as the T9 SSRF guard.

findings.title: Chat token grants PII-loaded AI access regardless of quote/itinerary status — no expiry/lifecycle check
findings.description: resolvePublicToken returns the resource status but the chat route never inspects it (sibling quote/select enforces status in ('sent','viewed')). A token for an expired/declined/withdrawn/accepted quote or past-sailing itinerary still resolves and loads customer PII context into an LLM conversation. Tokens are 256-bit random (not guessable) but never expire / not independently revocable.
findings.exploit_scenario: A quote link forwarded/scraped after the quote expired or was declined still opens an AI chat preloaded with the customer's trip/PII context indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Gate the chat route on resource status/expiry like quote/select, or add token_expires_at/token_revoked_at checked at resolve time.

findings.title: Concurrent booking-cancel double-counts clawback in platform_revenue (settled-payout branch has no CAS gate)
findings.description: The settled-payout clawback branch (payout.status in available|processing|paid) performs side effects with no atomic re-entry guard, unlike the pending branch (safeAwaitRowCount==1). Booking-cancel and commission-status are read-then-act; the negative platform_revenue insert has no idempotency key / ON CONFLICT / unique constraint, and the payout row is never moved off 'paid', so nothing blocks re-entry. Stripe createReversal is idempotent via key, but the ledger insert is not.
findings.exploit_scenario: Two concurrent POST /api/bookings/{id}/cancel for a booking whose commission is 'received' with a 'paid' payout: both pass the status reads, both insert a negative platform_revenue row → the §36 cancellation-revenue report double-counts the clawback.
findings.recommendation: Gate the clawback on an atomic CAS that claims the payout row (.update({status:'reversed'}).eq('id',payout.id).eq('status',payout.status).select('id') asserted to 1 row); proceed with reversal+ledger only when claimed, else 409. Or add a unique idempotency key on platform_revenue with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unthrottled OTP-issue route enables email-verification brute force / cross-session identity binding
findings.description: POST microsoft-email-prompt has no session check, no assertPermission, no rate limiter. It accepts an arbitrary email, mints a 6-digit OTP keyed ONLY by email (not session), resets attempts:0 each call, and sets _ms_pending_email. The verify route binds the email to whatever auth user the session resolves to (admin.updateUserById, email_confirm:true). Brute defense is only per-email MAX_OTP_ATTEMPTS=5 plus a per-IP limiter on verify only. Regenerating codes resets attempts, enabling unbounded guessing; membership/identity flows key on email.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker with their own OAuth session repeatedly prompts victim@corp.com (fresh OTP, attempts reset) and guesses codes on verify (IP-rotated); on a hit, victim's email is stamped onto the attacker's auth_user_id with email_confirm:true → identity claim.
findings.recommendation: Bind the OTP to the authenticated session (key by auth_user_id), require a session in the prompt route, add the per-IP limiter + a per-email regeneration cap to the prompt route, and back limiters with Redis.

findings.title: Anonymous chat endpoint streams raw error.message (DB/internal) to the client via SSE
findings.description: The chat POST serves anonymous traffic; handleChat runs service-role/tenant DB mutations + RAG. On any throw, void handleChat().catch streams err.message verbatim as an SSE 'error' event. supabase-js/Postgres errors embed table/column/constraint names. Issue #1125 pattern on the highest-volume unauthenticated surface.
findings.exploit_scenario: Unauthenticated visitor crafts input to trip a DB constraint during message persist; the SSE error frame returns the raw Postgres message, disclosing schema internals.
findings.recommendation: Log server-side with a random ref (reuse dbErrorResponse) and stream a generic message + ref; never relay err.message to an anonymous caller.

findings.title: Quote 'accepted' transition has no source-state guard
findings.description: Option-select unconditionally sets quotes.status='accepted' with no check on current status (unlike booking submit CAS or quote send 409). Tenant-scoped and permission-gated, so intra-tenant integrity gap, not cross-tenant.
findings.exploit_scenario: An agent (or replayed request) selects an option on a cancelled/expired/superseded quote; the container flips back to 'accepted' with fresh accepted_at, resurrecting a dead quote into downstream booking/commission flows.
findings.recommendation: CAS: .update(...).eq('id',quote_id).eq('tenant_id',ctx.tenant_id).in('status',['sent','draft']).select('id'); 409 on zero rows.

findings.title: line-item POST does not verify parent booking belongs to caller's tenant
findings.description: POST inserts booking_line_items with tenant_id=ctx (trusted) and booking_id from URL (untrusted) with no ownership SELECT on bookings, unlike the #715-hardened resources sibling. Injected tenant_id keeps the row in the attacker's tenant, so no direct cross-tenant read; risk is a dangling/cross-tenant booking_id reference + commission-math pollution unless a composite FK rejects it (not verified).
findings.exploit_scenario: Agent in tenant A POSTs to /api/bookings/<tenant-B-booking>/line-items; a line item is created in A referencing B's booking_id.
findings.recommendation: Mirror #715: SELECT bookings .eq('id',bookingId).eq('tenant_id',ctx.tenant_id).maybeSingle() and 404 before insert.

findings.title: Imported-commission gross uses native float multiply + Math.round, bypassing money.ts
findings.description: const gross = Math.round(commissionable * rate.rate) uses IEEE-754 multiply and Math.round, violating the §14.0.4 money.ts contract (big.js, half-away-from-zero). Currently dormant (subhost_payable_cents hard-coded 0, BYO phase), so no payout impact yet, but latent integrity drift.
findings.exploit_scenario: An imported booking whose fare×rate lands near an x.5 boundary rounds off-by-one-cent vs the rest of the system; becomes payout-affecting if sub-host imports are enabled.
findings.recommendation: Use multiplyRate(BigInt(commissionable), toRate(rate.rate)) from @/lib/money (satisfies atc/no-money-math).

findings.title: quote_options lookup not tenant-scoped — single-layer isolation on token-resolved write
findings.description: After resolving quote by token, the quote_options check queries by id alone and validates only optData.quote_id===quote.id; updates key on quote_id/id with no .eq('tenant_id',...). Single-layer (D-091 #4). Practically bounded by the quote_id match.
findings.exploit_scenario: Defense-in-depth gap: if a quote_options row's quote_id were cross-tenant-mismatched, the missing tenant filter removes the backstop containing the write.
findings.recommendation: Add .eq('tenant_id',quote.tenant_id) to the select and both updates.

findings.title: Resend webhook has no idempotency/dedup; re-delivery re-enqueues soft-bounce retry jobs
findings.description: Unlike the Stripe handler (atomic insert into stripe_webhook_events keyed on event id), the Resend handler never persists svix-id. Svix delivery is at-least-once; on email.bounced (soft) it unconditionally inngest.send the retry at attempt:1 each re-delivery. Status/suppression mutations are idempotent, so blast radius is duplicate jobs/retry emails. Not attacker-triggerable (valid Svix signature required).
findings.exploit_scenario: Legitimate Resend re-deliveries spawn multiple parallel soft-bounce retry chains, increasing outbound email to a bouncing address.
findings.recommendation: Persist svix-id in a resend_webhook_events dedup table (atomic insert-or-409) before dispatch, mirroring Stripe.

findings.title: relationship POST does not verify from/to contacts belong to caller's tenant
findings.description: POST inserts contact_relationships from from_contact_id (URL) and to_contact_id (body) via tenantClient (injects caller tenant_id). Neither contact UUID is verified within the caller's tenant before insert. Row lands in attacker's tenant; risk is edges referencing foreign contact UUIDs surfaced in the tenant-scoped GET (existence oracle) + AI relationship pollution.
findings.exploit_scenario: Agent in tenant A POSTs relationships with to_contact_id = a guessed tenant-B contact UUID; the edge persists and confirms the foreign UUID is valid.
findings.recommendation: SELECT both contacts via tenantClient and 404/400 if either is missing before insert.

findings.title: Unsubscribe HMAC tokens never expire (companion tokens do)
findings.description: signUnsubscribeToken/verifyUnsubscribeToken carry no exp (companion tokens enforce 90-day exp). HMAC-SHA256 signed, fail-closed key, timingSafeEqual — not forgeable. Residual: unlimited lifetime; token travels in URL query (referer/proxy logs), letting a captured link suppress that email/category forever.
findings.exploit_scenario: An unsubscribe URL captured from proxy logs is replayed any time later to suppress the victim's email for that tenant.
findings.recommendation: Stamp exp on unsubscribe payloads (mirror companion tokens); accept missing-exp for backward compat.

findings.title: Two admin GET routes read cross-tenant data via raw service-role without withPlatformAdminAudit
findings.description: admin/tenants and admin/platform-settings authenticate with a constant-time bearer compare (sound) but query via createServiceRoleClient() directly, not through withPlatformAdminAudit — so no audit_log row for these cross-tenant reads. They're also the only two routes not using the shared assertPlatformAdmin family.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker with MAIN_APP_ADMIN_API_KEY enumerates every tenant and reads all platform settings with zero forensic trail, delaying detection of key compromise.
findings.recommendation: Wrap both reads in withPlatformAdminAudit (admin_user_id:'service:bearer', reason) so the cross-tenant read lands an audit row.

findings.title: Gmail Pub/Sub history pointer advanced after the per-message loop; failure mid-loop reprocesses messages
findings.description: Pub/Sub JWT verified against Google JWKS (sound). Messages upserted by message_id (idempotent row write), but pubsub_history_id is advanced only after the loop; a failure after emitting import.queued but before the pointer update re-fetches the same history window and may re-emit import triggers (depends on processGmailInboundMessage dedup).
findings.exploit_scenario: Not attacker-triggerable. A failure between trigger-emission and pointer update reprocesses the same Gmail message, possibly queuing a duplicate import.
findings.recommendation: Confirm processGmailInboundMessage is idempotent per message_id (or gate import.queued on tenant_id+message_id).

findings.title: Office/PDF parsers fully decompress untrusted uploads before any output cap (zip-bomb amplification)
findings.description: extractContent dispatches uploads to mammoth/exceljs/officeparser/unpdf. OOXML files are ZIP containers fully decompressed in memory; only input caps (50MB RAG / 10MB imports) and a 1MB OUTPUT cap applied AFTER extraction exist. A ~50MB highly-compressible OOXML can expand to GBs before the cap, OOMing the function. Amplification, not plain volumetric DoS.
findings.exploit_scenario: Authenticated tenant member uploads a 30MB zip-bomb .xlsx (valid PK magic, under 50MB); workbook.xlsx.load inflates to GBs, OOMs/crashes the extraction worker.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a decompression-ratio / uncompressed-size guard (inspect central-directory sizes or streaming unzip with per-entry + total caps) before parsing; or hard memory/time budget treating OOM as failed.

findings.title: Proxy admin gate accepts any Supabase auth cookie shape; authority depends entirely on per-route assertPlatformAdmin
findings.description: isAcceptableAdminCredential passes /api/admin/* for any request with a valid-shaped Supabase auth cookie (shape check, not verification — deliberate). Authoritative authz is each route's assertPlatformAdmin. All 54 current admin routes assert; risk is structural fragility — a future admin route added without an in-handler assertion is reachable by any logged-in tenant user. (Also reported as F-adm-02.)
findings.exploit_scenario: A future /api/admin/new-thing route forgets assertPlatformAdmin; any authenticated viewer-role user's normal session cookie passes the middleware shape-check and the route runs with no role enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI guard (like check:permission-matrix) asserting every app/api/admin/**/route.ts references assertPlatformAdmin*/assertPlatformRole or the MAIN_APP_ADMIN_API_KEY constant-time compare.

findings.title: Stripe error path deletes the idempotency row before returning 500, relying on per-handler idempotency for safe replay
findings.description: On a handler exception, processing_outcome='error' is set then the stripe_webhook_events row is deleted and 500 returned so Stripe retries. Safe only if each event handler is internally idempotent. The financial RPC takes p_stripe_event_id (DB idempotent) and tenant updates are mostly fixed-value sets, but a partial-success-then-throw replays prior steps (relies on progressTo rejecting from the post-transition state).
findings.exploit_scenario: Not attacker-triggerable. A transient mid-handler failure causes full replay; a non-idempotent branch could double-apply.
findings.recommendation: Confirm every dispatch branch is replay-safe; consider keeping the errored row and gating reprocessing on outcome to detect prior partial progress.

findings.title: Nested-quantifier arithmetic regex run on AI candidate responses
findings.description: EXPR_REGEX has a token [\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?%? repeated inside (?:...)* applied to candidate_response (which an anon chat user can steer). Repetitions are separated by a required operator, which largely prevents exponential blowup; dominant cost is likely quadratic. Could not confirm catastrophic backtracking statically; input bounded by model max_tokens.
findings.exploit_scenario: Anon customer coaxes the assistant into emitting a long comma/digit+operator string with no closing '='; the supervisor runs EXPR_REGEX each response, adding CPU latency. Not a confirmed hang.
findings.recommendation: Cap scanned length (text.slice(0,20000)) and restructure the number token (\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*); add a bounded-time unit test on a pathological 10k-char input.

findings.title: Any tenant member can commit an un-claimed anonymous session in their tenant to their own account
findings.description: transfer-session commit only rejects if already transferred to a different user; if transferred_to_user_id is null, any active tenant member with a valid anonymous_session_id (tenant-scoped) can softCommitTransfer it onto their own user.id, re-keying that anon conversation's messages. No check that the caller originated the anon session. Bounded by the unguessable UUID + tenant scope.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tenant member who obtains another visitor's anonymous_session_id (shared link/log/referer) commits that stranger's anon conversation (possibly PII shared with the AI) to their own account.
findings.recommendation: Bind commit to proof of originating the anon session — compare the request's atc-anon-session cookie against the row.

findings.title: CruiseMapper DIY fetcher follows redirects with no internal-IP block (host not directly tenant-controlled)
findings.description: fetchCruiseMapperPage issues fetch() with default redirect-follow and no scheme/IP allowlist. URL is built from a fixed env base + internal IDs (cron-driven), so the initial host is operator-controlled — hence LOW. Residual: an upstream 30x redirect to an internal target would be followed unguarded.
findings.exploit_scenario: A compromised/redirecting upstream returns 302 to http://169.254.169.254/...; the fetcher follows it and returns the body. Requires control of the upstream response or base-URL env.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same SSRF guard as F-ssrf-01 (scheme allowlist, internal-IP block, redirect:'manual' with per-hop re-validation).

findings.title: Tenant scoping of storage path uses startsWith without traversal normalization
findings.description: Endpoint takes attacker-supplied path from query, authorizes via path.startsWith(`${ctx.tenant_id}/`), then passes verbatim to storage.createSignedUrl. A value like <tenant>/../<other>/x.pdf satisfies startsWith. Exploitable only if Supabase Storage normalizes '..' in keys (flat S3-style keyspace normally treats '..' literally) — not verified, hence low.
findings.exploit_scenario: If Supabase normalizes '..', a member could request path=<their_tenant>/../<victim_tenant>/<id>.pdf and get a signed URL to another tenant's document.
findings.recommendation: Reject path containing '..' or not matching ^<tenant_id>/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$, or derive path from a DB row looked up under the tenant filter.
